ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: the figure shows methanol H3C–OH located at the lower left, close to an O=C=N–S(=O)2Cl structure; a curved arrow goes from the methanol oxygen to the central carbon of the isocyanate, and another curved arrow indicates that the π electrons of C=N move to nitrogen. The sulfur on the right is connected to two oxygens and one chlorine, forming an –S(=O)2Cl group. Reasoning: according to the arrow pushing, the methanol oxygen attacks the central carbon of O=C=N–S(=O)2Cl, forming a C–OCH3 bond; the C=N π-bond electrons transfer to nitrogen, and N–H is obtained via proton transfer. The product connectivity is CH3O–C(=O)–NH–S(=O)2–Cl. Writing this structure as SMILES gives O=S(NC(OC)=O)(Cl)=O.

method.method_draft: Identify the atoms in the image: methanol attacks the central carbon of O=C=N–S(=O)2Cl. Apply the shown electron flow: form a C–OCH3 bond at the isocyanate carbon and convert the C=N linkage into an N–H single-bonded sulfonamide/carbamate linkage after proton relocation. The final molecule has connectivity CH3O–C(=O)–NH–S(=O)2–Cl. Encode that structure in SMILES as O=S(NC(OC)=O)(Cl)=O.
